interfaces: EvaluateMergeReadinessResult { taskId, revision, pullRequestNumber, ready, reasons }
MergeReadinessReason { code, message, role?, checkContext?, dependencyTaskId?, findingIds? }

MergeReadinessReasonCode = PULL_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND | PULL_REQUEST_HEAD_MISMATCH | PULL_REQUEST_BASE_MISMATCH | REVIEW_NOT_CURRENT_PASS | BLOCKING_FINDINGS_UNRESOLVED | CI_CHECK_NOT_SUCCESSFUL | DEPENDENCY_NOT_SATISFIED
MergeReadinessLifecycleStatePort.get(taskId) boundary onto control-plane.lifecycle-state-machine's persisted lifecycle records

MergeReadinessPrPort.findOpenPullRequests({ head }): Promise<readonly PullRequestRecord[]> boundary onto control-plane.pr-lifecycle's PullRequestRecord shape, discovering by head branch alone (never a server-side base filter)
MergeReadinessCiPort.listCheckRuns(ref, checkName): Promise<readonly CiCheckRunRecord[]> source-control/CI-status adapter boundary, queried once per required check name
CiCheckRunRecord { name, status, conclusion, startedAt } (status accepts any GitHub-reported string, not a closed enum)
GitHubCiStatusOperations(options) concrete MergeReadinessCiPort adapter over the GitHub REST Checks API's check_name-filtered endpoint
CiStatusProviderError { code, status } normalized GitHub-adapter failure
GitHubMergeReadinessPullRequestOperations(options) concrete MergeReadinessPrPort adapter over the GitHub REST pulls-list endpoint, head-only filtered
DEFAULT_REQUIRED_CI_CHECKS readonly string[] naming BOOT-023's two required GitHub Actions job/check-run names

behavioralConstraints: evaluate() resolves the task's canonical branch and exact current revision strictly through the unmodified control-plane.git-branch-lifecycle adapter; a Git branch mismatch or Git failure is normalized to BRANCH_REJECTED and no further check is performed

review/approval evidence is read through control-plane.review-rework's getApprovalStatus(), never re-derived from the evidence store's revision-matching logic directly; a failure reading it is normalized to EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE

getApprovalStatus() re-resolves the branch revision independently of the branch adapter call evaluate() already made; if the two disagree (the branch moved in between), the call is rejected as REVISION_CHANGED rather than computing readiness against a revision the returned evidence does not actually describe

the primary review-readiness signal is the task's own lifecycle record, read through MergeReadinessLifecycleStatePort.get(taskId): readiness requires currentState === MERGE_READY AND a history entry with toState === MERGE_READY and revisionIdentity === the resolved current revision; a missing record is treated as lifecycle state PLANNED; when this signal does not confirm readiness for the exact revision, evaluate() emits one TASK_NOT_MERGE_READY reason naming the observed currentState

when — and only when — the task is not confirmed MERGE_READY for the exact revision, every role reported by getApprovalStatus() other than MergeController is additionally checked as diagnostic detail: NONE, STALE, or a CURRENT non-PASS outcome each produce one REVIEW_NOT_CURRENT_PASS reason naming that role; when the task IS confirmed MERGE_READY for the exact revision, no per-role check runs at all — this specifically covers a task whose requiredReviewRoles needs no independent QA/Architecture/UAT stage, for which control-plane.review-rework never writes a Developer review-result bridge and getApprovalStatus() would otherwise report Developer: NONE forever

a role whose current approval is CURRENT with a non-PASS outcome (only evaluated per the previous constraint) additionally has its current ipt.review-result record read through control-plane.evidence-store; any finding in that record at severity MEDIUM, HIGH, or CRITICAL produces one BLOCKING_FINDINGS_UNRESOLVED reason naming that role and every such findingId; a role's STALE or NONE approval never triggers this check, since a stale/absent record's findings do not describe the current revision

every taskId in the task's declared dependencies array is checked through MergeReadinessLifecycleStatePort.get(); a missing record is treated as lifecycle state PLANNED; any dependency whose state is not exactly DONE produces one DEPENDENCY_NOT_SATISFIED reason naming that dependency taskId; dependencies are checked in ascending lexical taskId order for deterministic reason ordering

listCheckRuns(revision, checkName) is called once per required check name (the dependencies-configured requiredCiChecks, defaulting to DEFAULT_REQUIRED_CI_CHECKS), filtering server-side via GitHub's own check_name parameter rather than fetching one unfiltered page of every check run on the revision, so a revision with more check runs than a single page cannot hide a required context past the first page; the returned runs are filtered defensively by exact name match and the one with the lexically greatest startedAt is treated as authoritative; a check name with no matching run, or whose latest run is not status=completed with conclusion=success, produces one CI_CHECK_NOT_SUCCESSFUL reason naming that check context; a run's status is accepted as any non-empty string GitHub reports (queued/in_progress/completed/waiting/requested/pending/etc.), never validated against a closed enum, since only exact equality with 'completed' is ever tested

findOpenPullRequests() is called once per evaluate() call with only the task's resolved canonical branch as head — never a server-side base filter, since GitHub's own base filter would silently exclude an open PR targeting the wrong base before this module could ever classify it; zero results produce exactly one PULL_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND reason with pullRequestNumber null; more than one result is rejected as PR_STATE_CONFLICT without evaluating any further pull-request reason; exactly one result is inspected locally against the configured integrationTarget (default 'main') for PULL_REQUEST_BASE_MISMATCH (its baseRef differs) and PULL_REQUEST_HEAD_MISMATCH (its headSha differs from the resolved current revision), each producing its own reason when true

ready is exactly reasons.length === 0; there is no request field, override parameter, or free-text justification that can set ready=true while any reason remains — every reason is computed solely from the typed dependency ports listed above

GitHubCiStatusOperations maps every non-2xx GitHub response to a CiStatusProviderError whose code is derived from the HTTP status (401 -> AUTH_FAILED, 403 -> RATE_LIMITED when the response message matches /rate limit/i, otherwise AUTH_FAILED, 404 -> NOT_FOUND, 429 -> RATE_LIMITED, any other non-2xx -> PROVIDER_ERROR) and whose status field carries the exact HTTP status; a transport-level failure (the fetch call itself rejecting) is mapped to NETWORK_FAILED with no status; a 2xx response whose JSON body is missing a required check_runs array, or whose entries are missing a required field, is mapped to PROVIDER_ERROR
GitHubMergeReadinessPullRequestOperations maps GitHub HTTP status to a PullRequestProviderError (BOOT-022's own error type) using the same 401/403/404/422/429 mapping BOOT-022 already documents

MergeReadinessPolicyEngine never inspects a CiStatusProviderError's or PullRequestProviderError's HTTP status or GitHub-specific payload shape directly; it only wraps the already-normalized provider error as CI_PROVIDER_FAILED or PR_PROVIDER_FAILED
GitHubCiStatusOperations and GitHubMergeReadinessPullRequestOperations each reject an empty owner, repo, or token at construction with a RangeError rather than deferring to a failed first request
invariants: this module performs no lifecycle-state transition, no merge, and no QA/Architecture/UAT/MergeController judgment; it only reads already-recorded evidence and provider state and computes a deterministic readiness boolean plus typed reasons from it

task-domain logic (MergeReadinessPolicyEngine) depends only on the MergeReadinessApprovalPort/MergeReadinessEvidencePort/MergeReadinessLifecycleStatePort/MergeReadinessPrPort/MergeReadinessCiPort interfaces, never on GitHub-specific request/response payloads or on the internal storage layout of any dependency module
evaluate() writes no evidence, PR, or lifecycle state; it is a pure read-only query and is safe to call repeatedly with no side effect

a branch, evidence, lifecycle-state, provider, or duplicate-pull-request-conflict failure is reported as a thrown MergeReadinessError before any reason is computed for that check, rather than folding an unreadable/ambiguous precondition into a 'not ready' reason; only a genuinely evaluable state produces reasons

for identical dependency-port responses, evaluate() always returns byte-for-byte identical output (reason order is fixed: the task's own MERGE_READY-for-revision check and any per-role diagnostic detail first, then dependencies in ascending lexical order, then CI checks in configured order, then pull-request identity last)
examples: a task whose own lifecycle record is MERGE_READY with a history entry bound to the exact current revision, whose declared dependencies are all DONE, whose required CI checks are both completed/success for the exact revision, and whose canonical open pull request's head/base match the resolved revision/integration target returns ready=true with an empty reasons array

a task whose QA/Architecture/UAT reviews all recorded PASS but whose review gate crashed before persisting the DEV_VALIDATED -> ... -> MERGE_READY lifecycle transition returns ready=false with a TASK_NOT_MERGE_READY reason (naming the task's actual, earlier currentState) rather than ready=true, because this module trusts BOOT-009's own authoritative transition record over re-deriving the same conclusion from possibly-incomplete role evidence

a task whose requiredReviewRoles is only Developer (or Developer plus MergeController) — for which control-plane.review-rework never bridges a Developer review-result, since only the QA/Architecture/UAT gates do — reaches ready=true once its own lifecycle record shows MERGE_READY bound to the exact revision, without ever needing that bridge to exist

a pull request whose head commit does not match the resolved current revision (for example a push landed after the task last reached MERGE_READY) returns ready=false with a PULL_REQUEST_HEAD_MISMATCH reason, even though the task's own lifecycle record is still MERGE_READY for the earlier commit

a task not yet MERGE_READY whose requiredReviewRoles includes Architect but has no recorded Architect review returns ready=false with both a TASK_NOT_MERGE_READY reason and a REVIEW_NOT_CURRENT_PASS reason naming Architect

a task whose 'Build and test (Node)' check run's latest attempt for the exact revision has conclusion=failure returns ready=false with a CI_CHECK_NOT_SUCCESSFUL reason naming that check context, independent of the 'Schema and contract validation (Python)' check's own result

a check run reporting status=waiting (a valid GitHub Checks status this module does not special-case) is treated the same as any other not-yet-completed status: CI_CHECK_NOT_SUCCESSFUL, not a parse failure of the whole provider response

a QA review whose current outcome is FAIL and whose recorded findings include one HIGH-severity entry returns both a REVIEW_NOT_CURRENT_PASS and a BLOCKING_FINDINGS_UNRESOLVED reason for QA, the latter naming that exact findingId
a task depending on BOOT-015 while BOOT-015's own lifecycle record is IN_DEVELOPMENT (not DONE) returns ready=false with a DEPENDENCY_NOT_SATISFIED reason naming BOOT-015

an open pull request from the task's canonical branch targeting 'develop' instead of 'main' is discovered (head-only filtering finds it regardless of its actual base) and returns ready=false with a PULL_REQUEST_BASE_MISMATCH reason, rather than PULL_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND

two open pull requests already existing for the same head branch (created out of band, regardless of their individual bases) cause evaluate() to fail as PR_STATE_CONFLICT rather than picking one arbitrarily to compute readiness against
edgeCases: an unregistered taskId is rejected as TASK_NOT_FOUND
a non-schema-valid taskId is rejected as INVALID_REQUEST before any dependency is touched
a Git branch mismatch reported by the branch adapter is normalized to BRANCH_REJECTED rather than propagating a raw BranchLifecycleError
an approval-status or evidence-store read failure is normalized to EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE rather than propagating a raw error
getApprovalStatus() resolving a different revision than the branch adapter already resolved is rejected as REVISION_CHANGED
a lifecycle-state read failure — for the task itself or for a dependency taskId — is normalized to LIFECYCLE_STATE_UNAVAILABLE rather than propagating a raw error
a task (or a dependency taskId) with no persisted lifecycle record at all is treated as PLANNED (not DONE, not MERGE_READY), the same convention BOOT-008's next-task selection already documents

a task whose lifecycle record is currentState=MERGE_READY but whose history has no entry binding that transition to the exact current revision (a later commit landed without a new rework/review cycle) falls back to the per-role diagnostic check rather than trusting a stale MERGE_READY label

zero open pull requests for the resolved head branch produces a PULL_REQUEST_NOT_FOUND reason (not a thrown error), since a task legitimately has no pull request yet before control-plane.pr-lifecycle has ever ensured one
a GitHub response body that parses as JSON but has no check_runs array, or whose check-run entries omit a required field, is treated as PROVIDER_ERROR
two check runs sharing the same name for the same revision (a rerun) are resolved to the one with the lexically greatest startedAt, never summed or averaged

allowedDependencies: control-plane.pr-lifecycle (PullRequestRecord shape and PullRequestProviderError type reuse only)

expectations: BOOT-025 can call evaluate() for the exact task/revision it is about to merge and treat ready=true as the sole deterministic precondition for proceeding, and ready=false's reasons as the exact, typed, human-and-machine-readable explanation for why it must not, without this module ever executing a merge or transitioning lifecycle state itself

a MergeController role review submitted afterward (schemas/v1/review-result.schema.json's mergeControllerDetails.policyChecks/blockingPrerequisites) can be populated directly from this module's reasons without BOOT-025 re-deriving them
acceptedRanges: an EvaluateMergeReadinessResult whose ready is exactly reasons.length === 0, for any combination of the typed MergeReadinessReasonCode values
requiredReachableRanges: ready=true is reachable for a task whose exact-revision evidence genuinely satisfies every gate
ready=false is reachable, with the specific reason(s) present, for a task whose exact-revision evidence genuinely violates any one gate
